sec_21_5_02.summary: LogSubject.NormalizeFileName removes Unicode Cc scalars only (Rune.IsControl), so Cf format characters (reproduced with U+202E RIGHT-TO-LEFT OVERRIDE, U+200B ZERO WIDTH SPACE, U+2066/U+2069 isolates) and the Zl/Zp separators U+2028/U+2029 pass verbatim into the operator-facing log. Bounded (128 scalars), no secret, no volume amplification (the throttle keys on category plus the code-owned event, never on the message).
sec_21_5_02.required_fix: Extend the removal predicate to the non-printing/invisible categories, at minimum Cf and Zl/Zp, and record the exact category set in the ADR-026 implementation note and the architecture documentation.

sec_21_5_03.summary: LogSubject.Create uses Path.GetFileName, so on the pinned Linux host a backslash is a legal file-name character and 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv' and '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv' are emitted whole (32/32 and 34/34 scalars), disclosing a user account name and a full directory chain contrary to ADR-026 clause 1's directory/full-path exclusion. Bounded, no secret.
sec_21_5_03.required_fix: Take the final path component by splitting on both '/' and '\\' regardless of host platform, then re-run the empty/whitespace/control-reduced fallback check on the extracted component.

work: In LogSubject.Create, replace the host-platform Path.GetFileName call with a platform-independent extraction of the final path component: take the substring after the last '/' and after the last '\\' (whichever is later), so a POSIX path, a Windows path, a UNC path, and a mixed-separator path all yield the same final component on every host. Re-run the empty/whitespace check on the extracted component before normalization, and keep the existing post-normalization fallback check, so a path that is only separators, or whose component reduces to nothing, still falls back to the item identifier in D format. Do not change the single-argument Create(Guid) overload's behavior.

In LogSubject.NormalizeFileName, extend the removal predicate from 'Rune.IsControl(rune)' (Unicode Cc) to the documented set of non-printing categories: at minimum Cc, Cf (format: U+200B/U+200D, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069, U+00AD, and the bidi controls), Zl (U+2028), and Zp (U+2029). Keep the existing single scalar-wise pass, the MaximumScalarValues=128 bound applied after removal, the never-split-surrogate-pair guarantee, and the never-collapse-or-trim whitespace behavior. State the exact category set in the XML doc comments on the helper so the policy is code-documented, and decide explicitly (and record the decision and its reason) whether any other category is in scope; if a category is judged ambiguous, exclude it and say why rather than leaving it implicit.

Preserve every existing LogSubjectTests invariant, including the 23 existing cases: the positive POSIX controls, the non-ASCII verbatim cases (/media/日本語/お気に入りの映画.mkv, Amélie, the decomposed 'Cafe\u0301', and the astral-plane 'Movie 🎬.mkv'), the 128-scalar bound applied after removal, the surrogate-pair integrity case, the no-whitespace-collapse case, and the three empty/whitespace/control-only fallback cases. A change that strips a combining mark, a letter, or an emoji is a regression, not a hardening.

Add failing-on-pre-fix tests in tests/ArrTags.Tests/LogSubjectTests.cs for SEC-21.5-02: a Theory over the reproduced scalars (U+202E, U+200B, U+2066/U+2069, U+2028, U+2029) asserting none survives into the subject, plus a positive control proving an ordinary Cc control IS still stripped, plus a non-ASCII/astral positive control proving nothing else is stripped.

Add failing-on-pre-fix tests for SEC-21.5-03: 'C:\\Users\\admin\\Videos\\secret.mkv' and '\\\\fileserver\\media\\secret\\file.mkv' must each yield only the final component with no account name and no directory separator anywhere in the subject; a mixed-separator path must behave the same; the existing POSIX cases must be unchanged; and the URL-shaped SR-15.4-04 observation (a query string on a file-name-shaped path is retained, and Path.GetFileName is a path splitter, not a URL parser) must be covered by an explicit test that documents the retained behavior as unchanged, so it is neither silently altered nor silently dropped.

decision_gates.note: DG-22 is resolved by the user decision recorded by ADR-026 (Accepted (v1.2)). risks: Over-removal: a category added to the predicate that a legitimate media file name uses (a combining mark in Mn, a private-use glyph, a regional-indicator pair) silently corrupts the operator's correlation key. The non-ASCII verbatim tests and the 128-scalar bound tests are the guard; the predicate's category set must be stated explicitly, not accumulated ad hoc.

Under-removal: leaving a category out (for example a deprecated bidi control, a Hangul filler, or a non-Cc, non-Cf, non-Zl/Zp whitespace-like separator) leaves the same class of finding open and the 21.14 review will report it. The task's own acceptance criterion is that no reproduced non-printing scalar survives, so the set is validated by the reviewer's reproductions, not by the worker's list alone.

The dual-separator split could change a currently-correct subject: a POSIX file name that legitimately contains a backslash is legal on Linux, and splitting on '\\' truncates it. That is the intended fail-toward-safety direction (a shorter subject, never a longer one) and is called out in the ADR note so the behavior is documented rather than surprising.

A file name that consists only of non-printing scalars must still fall back to the item id, not to an empty subject; the post-normalization fallback check is the only thing that guarantees this, so it must not be 'simplified away' while the predicate grows.

Widening the predicate changes golden-independent log output, so LogRedactionTests or a bounded-output assertion in another suite may need updating; a change there is only acceptable if the new expectation is strictly more restrictive.
